caption:
are the dots on my nose blackheads or sebaceous filaments?

Many of the small grey or beige dots on the nose are not blackheads. They are sebaceous filaments - a normal column of oil and skin cells inside each follicle. They are common, especially on the nose and centre of the face in people with oilier skin and visible pores.

How to tell them apart in the mirror:

Sebaceous filaments: small, flat, evenly spread, light grey to beige. Squeezed, they come out as a pale thread.

Blackheads: fewer, darker, with a wider opening and a firmer plug. They are a form of acne.

The part pore strips don't mention: once a filament is removed, the follicle fills again - within about 30 days in the classic study that first described them. That is not a failure. It is the follicle doing its job.

What this does not mean: that description dates from 1976, and you can't tell everything from a mirror. Squeezing hard every week mainly adds irritation. If the dots are inflamed, painful or changing, that is a different conversation.

Plewig G, Wolff HH. Arch Dermatol Res 1976. doi:10.1007/BF00581673
